contexts.text: Who hath not forsaken His mercy () = the perception of the influx of love.
I will leave thee in the wilderness (.) = devoid of truths and goods. AE 654:52.
Multitude is predicated of truths, which are said to be forsaken () when they are not. AE 730:6.

By men are signified those who are in falsities; and by women, those who are in evils from the affection of falsity; because it is said, that the one shall be taken and the other left (); that is, that those who are in truths from affection will be saved, and that those who are in evils from affection will be condemned. AE 810:2. AE 1182:3.
As, from this, comes the devastation of all good and truth, it is said, a place forsaken to the nettle ().
They have forsaken Jehovah, and have provoked the Holy One of Israel () = that they have rejected Divine good and Divine truth.
